title: Design Circular Queue
description:
# Design Circular Queue

Design a fixed-capacity circular queue named `MyCircularQueue`. A circular queue stores elements in first-in-first-out order, but when the physical storage reaches the end it wraps back to the beginning and reuses slots that were freed by previous dequeues.

Implement the `MyCircularQueue` class:

* `MyCircularQueue(int k)` initializes the queue with capacity `k`.
* `boolean enQueue(int value)` inserts `value` at the rear if the queue is not full, and returns whether the insert succeeded.
* `boolean deQueue()` removes the front element if the queue is not empty, and returns whether the removal succeeded.
* `int Front()` returns the front value, or `-1` when the queue is empty.
* `int Rear()` returns the rear value, or `-1` when the queue is empty.
* `boolean isEmpty()` returns whether the queue currently has no elements.
* `boolean isFull()` returns whether the queue currently has exactly `k` elements.

The key behavior is slot reuse: after you remove elements from the front, later enqueues must be able to wrap around and occupy those freed positions. Do not use a built-in queue implementation.

In operation examples, the first array lists operations and the second lists their argument lists, paired by index and executed left to right. The first operation constructs the object; later operations use that same object. Outputs align by index too: constructors and void methods produce `null`; an empty argument list `[]` means no arguments.

## Example 1

**Input:**
["MyCircularQueue", "enQueue", "enQueue", "enQueue", "enQueue", "Rear", "isFull", "deQueue", "enQueue", "Rear"]
[[3], [1], [2], [3], [4], [], [], [], [4], []]

**Output:**
[null, true, true, true, false, 3, true, true, true, 4]

**Explanation:**
The fourth insert fails because the capacity is 3. After one dequeue frees the front slot, inserting 4 succeeds and becomes the new rear.

## Constraints

* `1 <= k <= 1000`
* `0 <= value <= 1000`
* At most `3000` calls will be made to `enQueue`, `deQueue`, `Front`, `Rear`, `isEmpty`, and `isFull`.

examples.output: [null, true, true, true, false, 3, true, true, true, 4]

solutions.name: Counted Circular Array
solutions.description:
## Approach
Use an array of length `k`, a `front` index, and a `size` counter. The next rear position is `(front + size) % capacity`, so inserting after a dequeue naturally wraps into freed slots.

## Key Insight
The `size` counter makes empty and full states unambiguous: empty means `size == 0`, full means `size == capacity`. The array index only describes where data lives physically.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(1) per operation
- Space Complexity: O(k)

solutions.name: One Empty Slot Ring Buffer
solutions.description:
## Approach
Allocate `k + 1` slots and always leave one slot unused. `front` points at the current front value and `rear` points at the next write position.

## Key Insight
Without a `size` counter, `front == rear` could mean either empty or full. The spare slot removes that ambiguity: empty is `front == rear`, and full is `(rear + 1) % data.length == front`.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(1) per operation
- Space Complexity: O(k)

solutions.name: Monotonic Index Ring Buffer
solutions.description:
## Approach
Keep two increasing counters, `head` and `tail`, instead of wrapping the counters themselves. Physical array positions are `head % capacity` and `tail % capacity`.

## Key Insight
The logical size is `tail - head`. This makes the state checks simple while still using a fixed circular array for storage.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(1) per operation
- Space Complexity: O(k)

solutions.name: Object Linked List Queue
solutions.description:
## Approach
Use a singly linked list with `head` and `tail` node references, plus `size` and `capacity`. Enqueue appends a new node at the tail, and dequeue removes the head node.

## Key Insight
A circular queue is an interface contract, not necessarily an array-only implementation. The capacity check still enforces at most `k` live nodes, and head/tail references make all operations constant time.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(1) per operation
- Space Complexity: O(k) live nodes

solutions.name: Preallocated Linked Ring Nodes
solutions.description:
## Approach
Create `k` node objects once and link them into a ring. `read` points to the front position, `write` points to the next slot to fill, and `lastWritten` remembers the rear value.

## Key Insight
This keeps the linked-node model but reuses exactly the same `k` storage cells forever, making wrap-around explicit without using array indexes for queue logic.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(1) per operation
- Space Complexity: O(k)

tests.output: [null, true, true, true, false, 3, true, true, true, 4]

tests.description: Empty queue operations, full detection, and wrap-around enqueue.
Capacity-one queue must distinguish empty and full after each operation.
Repeated enqueue/dequeue cycles must reuse storage instead of consuming a fresh slot forever.
Front and rear remain correct after wrap-around and partial removal.
Empty and full flags must update across alternating state transitions.
Failed enqueue after a wrapped full state must not overwrite the existing front or rear.
Boundary values 0 and 1000 must be preserved through front and rear queries.
